external_authority.source: Jansen and Scheffler, Generalized coloring for tree-like graphs
external_authority.statement: List Coloring on trees is solvable in linear time.
Repeated singleton propagation; empty list gives NO; if all lists in a forest have size at least 2, the instance is YES.

theorem.input: Forest F with arbitrary finite lists L(v).
algorithm: Apply exact singleton propagation to a fixpoint.
If any list becomes empty, return UNSAT.
Otherwise every remaining list has size at least 2.
Every remaining forest component is list-colorable by leaf induction.

equivalent_DP.recurrence: F(v)={c in L(v): for every child u there exists d in F(u) with d!=c}
equivalent_DP.criterion: F(root) nonempty for every tree root
equivalent_DP.reconstruction: Choose a root color in F(root) and recurse to child colors different from the parent color.

exact_use_condition: The residual interaction graph is a forest.
All restrictions induced by fixed/precolored boundary vertices have already been encoded into the current lists.
applicability_to_C11_PI.conclusion: Residual feasibility is polynomially decidable without a general P7-free 4-coloring oracle.
